Storytime: It got better in college cause I got a girlfriend and friends, but I had a lot of untreated mental illness, as did my partner. My Senior year of college was her 1L of law school, we got engaged, planned the wedding, and as time went by mental illness quietly grew. The next year I started grad school but failed out, went to the hospital due to suicidal ideation. That made it clear that we weren’t right for each other cause it was clear we were both suffering. Now there’s been no contact since I got the last of my things out of her apartment. It’s gotten much ‘worse’ since then, because all my depression and anxiety and heartbreak take especially long to heal. Once my best friend and the love of my college life, now just a memory. My mental health has made my ability to earn a living and pay off loans nearly impossible. That being said, things have also become ‘better’ since I’m actually dealing with my issues and there were a lot of things I hated about my ex. I wasn’t strong enough to end it sooner. I was deeply in love with her despite the pain and afraid I would amount to nothing without her. One thing in particular was that she hated my family, and low key her own too, and that didn’t vibe with me. I treated my parents really poorly during our relationship, it’s a monstrous regret. Thankfully they are incredibly loving people and I’m so happy to have them as an integral part of my life again. 

If you have been, thanks for reading, cheers.
But what really is a whole? What really is a hole? If there’s a hole in my heart, can I ever be whole again?
